correctness.rationale: The stationary reset age is exactly Exp(r). A deterministic hydrodynamic first integral gives the positive scale density alpha exp(-alpha F)F_prime. Weighted density at spatial coordinate z is B_z(U). Monotone likelihood ratios make the B_z-weighted expectation of U strictly decreasing; its endpoints bracket E(U), proving one and only one sign transition. For rapid resetting, covariance identities yield Var(U)/Cov(U,U^3)->1/3; for slow resetting, explicit scaled integrals yield m~alpha L, I1(z_k)~alpha log L and I2(z_k)~2alpha/(3 z_k), forcing the coefficient 2/3 in z_*~2/(3alpha L log L). Stationary normalization, positivity and numerical boundaries are checked by standalone quadrature, but the proof does not infer infinite statements from finite checks.

value.rationale: The source studies a repulsive condensate in which global resetting produces dynamically emergent fluctuations. Local density covariance between the center and observation radius is a natural spatial two-point measurement not captured by the averaged profile or a single centered-window counting distribution. The theorem proves a unique positive-to-negative transition and a measurable qualitative change of its location from inside the original cloud at rapid resetting to far outside at slow resetting, with a sharp inverse-log and inverse-loglog law. It separates macroscopic reset-age anticorrelations from microscopic quantum correlations without requiring an unrelated arbitrary slice or general conjecture.
